user.title: NeoSmartBlinds hub
user.description: Point this at your NeoSmartBlinds controller. TCP on port 8839 is recommended: the HTTP path derives its deduplication hash from the microsecond clock, which is weaker than the vendor recommends and can silently drop a frame. Add your blinds afterwards from the integration options.

data.name: Name
data.hub_id: Hub ID (the 24 character controller ID from the app)

init.title: NeoSmartBlinds options
init.description: Add, edit or remove blinds, and tune the command timing and repeats. Choose Save changes when you are done, or close without saving to discard.

add_blind.title: Add a blind
add_blind.description: The blind code and motor code come from the NeoSmartBlinds app. Every bf motor blind must carry its motor code (usually bf). Set close time to the real measured full travel, timed with a stopwatch.

data.start_position: Start position, percent open, only used in a positioning mode

add_button.title: Add a button control
add_button.description: Map one press of a physical button to an action on a group of blinds. Pressing it drives the whole group together, so the hub coalesces them into one command and two buttons pressed together move their walls in parallel, with no mutex or waiting. Point the event entity at the button channel, and set the press type to match its event_type attribute (check it in Developer Tools if unsure).

data.name: Name
data.event_type: Press type (must match the entity's event_type, for example press, double_press, single_push)
data.cooldown: Cooldown after travel (seconds, presses inside this window are ignored)
data.travel_ceiling: Travel ceiling (seconds, the longest a press waits for the group to stop)

data.cooldown: Cooldown after travel (seconds, presses inside this window are ignored)
data.travel_ceiling: Travel ceiling (seconds, the longest a press waits for the group to stop)

tuning.title: Command timing and repeats
tuning.description: The RF to these motors is lossy, so open and close commands are re-sent on an escalating schedule until every blind catches a frame. The schedule is a comma separated list of seconds, each value being the wait after the previous attempt (the default spreads eight attempts across about seventeen minutes). Leave it blank to switch repeats off. The repeats are safe at any length: a blind never receives two repeats driving it opposite ways. Never set the command backoff below 0.5 seconds, the hub needs that long to process each frame.

data.repeat_schedule: Repeat schedule (seconds, comma separated, blank to disable)
data.favourite_repeat_multipliers: Favourite repeat schedule (multiples of a full travel, comma separated; the favourite is the least reliable command so it needs several; blank to disable)
data.favourite_idle_guard: Favourite idle guard, seconds a blind must be stopped before gp
data.favourite_settle_timeout: Favourite settle timeout, seconds to wait for a moving blind before gp
data.log_commands: Log every transmitted command at info level

set_favourite.name: Set favourite
set_favourite.description: Send the blind to its single stored favourite position (gp), waiting for it to be stationary first.

send_command.name: Send raw command
send_command.description: Send a raw motor command straight to the blind, for troubleshooting.

command.name: Command
command.description: The two character motor command to send (for example up, dn, sp, gp).
